newsitem.title: UK: British bullying victim wins compensation.
newsitem.headline: British bullying victim wins compensation.

text.p: A young British man has won 30,000 pounds ($50,000) in compensation for alleged bullying at his London school in what is believed to be the first such successful case in Britain.

Sebastian Sharp, 20, claimed he was beaten up, verbally abused and tied up with string by other pupils at his state school during a four-year bullying ordeal which made him anxious, depressed and suicidal.
The school never accepted Sharp's allegations but their insurers offered him an out of court settlement on Friday to prevent costly legal proceedings.
"We were well prepared to fight the case in court and we were confident of a successful outcome," headmaster Simon Williams told BBC radio on Saturday.
"It is a matter of concern that we were unable to challenge these allegations that have been made. It has gone through without us being able to do that," Williams added.
Previous attempts to pursue cases of bullying in British courts have been thrown out.
Lawyers are expecting the case to prompt a flood of other legal claims by young people claiming that schools have been negligent in failing to protect them from bullying.
Sharp's lawyer James Rabinowitz told reporters he was preparing a further 10 claims against various schools.
Britain's education ministry launched a campaign against bullying in 1994 and expects schools to work out their own policies on how to deal with the problem. ($1=.6005 Pound)
